# Excellence 2026: Cloud Modernization Solutions in Action


November 02, 2026


by Craig Patton


##


A strong foundation is essential to modernizing government technology. Aging infrastructure, growing data demands, limited IT resources, and systems that require increasing effort to maintain make it harder for public-sector organizations to support critical operations and the services their communities depend on.


Moving to the cloud gives organizations an opportunity to rethink that foundation. By migrating existing solutions or implementing new technology directly in the cloud, governments can improve reliability, reduce infrastructure burdens, strengthen their ability to scale, and create a platform for continued modernization.


## Celebrating Excellence in Cloud Modernization Solutions


For 2027, the[Tyler Excellence Awards](https://www.tylertech.com/about-us/tyler-client-difference/tyler-excellence-awards) are introducing a Cloud Modernization category to recognize organizations strengthening their technology foundations through the cloud. While the category is new, Tyler clients were already demonstrating these outcomes in their 2026 award-winning stories across other categories. The examples below show how cloud modernization can strengthen critical operations today while creating a foundation for what comes next.


## Building a More Stable Foundation for Growth


[Fort Bend Central Appraisal District](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/fort-bend-cad-boosts-stability-with-saas-migration) , Texas, transitioned Assessment & Tax Pro to a Tyler‑hosted cloud environment to support rapid growth and reduce on‑premises security risks. The shift:


- Offloaded routine maintenance, updates, and security patching
- Avoided new storage costs
- Reduced extended downtime periods


“The improved stability has had a positive impact on employee morale and productivity, allowing staff to work with confidence in a reliable and dependable environment,” said Tiffany Benjebbour, chief of special projects.


## Creating the Foundation for Continued Modernization


The city of[Redondo Beach, California](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/podcast-episodes/redondo-beachs-cloud-journey-to-automation-readiness) , modernized their aging ERP environment by moving to cloud-based Enterprise ERP to reduce risk and improve efficiency. The city:


- Retired legacy servers and eliminated unsupported infrastructure
- Grew automation and self-service tools
- Reduced ERP outages from monthly to near zero
- Expanded Tyler’s Cashiering to three departments and enabled ACH payments
- Cut cybersecurity risk for systems containing financial, payroll, and personally identifiable information


“The time that was spent keeping the old system alive and going is now being spent on modernizing,” said Mike Cook, IT director.


## Protecting the Continuity of Justice


Previously constrained by on-premises infrastructure,[Peoria County, Illinois](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/standing-still-was-a-risk-to-justice-peoria-county-chose-cloud) , moved their mission-critical justice systems — jail, juvenile center, state attorney’s office, and circuit courts — to a modern environment. In the cloud, they:


- Established a secure judicial foundation built for scalability
- Delivered uninterrupted access to court dockets and electronic records
- Enhanced data flow from jail to prosecution to court
- Shifted focus from server maintenance to innovation support


“Our justice system is too critical to fail,” said Mark Little, chief information officer. “Our move to the cloud was a deliberate operational evolution to ensure we uphold our responsibility to justice.”


## Strengthening Reliability for Public Safety


[Hidalgo County, Texas](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/blog-articles/hidalgo-turns-to-the-cloud-for-faster-reliable-systems) , supports a network of law enforcement and public safety agencies that depend on reliable access to information. Adoption of cloud-hosted Enterprise Public Safety has:


- Improved workflows due to increased integration between departments
- Strengthened system reliability with 99.9% system availability achieved
- Laid the groundwork for future advanced initiatives like the “Field Arrest to Pre-Booking Alliance” project


“Our goal is to continue building a connected system that supports collaboration across departments and helps create a strong foundation for the next phase,” said Clarissa Longoria, senior IT manager.
